meta.titre: Factors of Production: land, labour, capital and enterprise and what each earns
meta.sous_theme: Four factors, their rewards, efficiency of labour and indirect production

sections.contenu_markdown: A woman in Mbouda who grows maize rents a plot, pays two helpers, buys a sprayer and decides herself what to plant and when to sell. Without noticing it, she is using all four factors of production. Every good and every service on sale, from a loaf of bread in Yaounde to a taxi ride in Douala, needs these same four ingredients. GCE papers ask for the meaning of each factor, the way labour differs from the others, what makes workers efficient, and the meaning of indirect production.

items: Production is the creation of goods and services that satisfy human wants.
Resources are scarce, so people must choose how to use them.
A consumer good is used directly to satisfy wants; a capital good is used to make other goods.

sections.titre: The factors of production and the efficiency of labour
sections.contenu_markdown:
### The four factors of production
Production needs resources, called factors of production. Each factor earns a reward for the person who supplies it.

| Factor | Meaning | Examples | Reward |
|---|---|---|---|
| Land | All natural resources provided by nature, not made by people | Soil, forests, rivers, minerals, fishing grounds | Rent |
| Labour | The physical and mental effort of human beings used in production | A farmer, a teacher, a driver, a nurse | Wages or salaries |
| Capital | Man-made goods used to produce other goods and services | Tools, machines, factory buildings, delivery trucks | Interest |
| Enterprise | The organising, decision-making and risk-taking factor | The business owner who combines the other three | Profit |

The entrepreneur brings the other factors together and bears the risk of making a loss.

### Special features of labour
Land and capital can be bought, owned and sold. Labour cannot be separated from the worker, so an employer can only hire a person's services for a period and pay wages for them. The worker also has feelings, gets tired, can refuse to move to another town and can go on strike. For these reasons labour is treated differently from land and capital.

### Efficiency and productivity of labour
The efficiency (productivity) of labour is the output produced by one worker in a given period of time:

$$\text{Productivity of labour} = \frac{\text{total output}}{\text{number of workers}}$$

It rises with better education and training, good health and feeding, better tools and machines, good working conditions, motivation, and the division of labour.

### Indirect production
Indirect production means making capital goods first and using them later to make consumer goods. It needs people to give up some present consumption. A fisherman who spends several days making a net, instead of fishing, is using indirect production.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the command word is define or state the meaning of
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give one clear sentence that says what the term is, then a short example. A two-mark definition usually earns one mark for the idea and one for precision or an example.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks how easily a factor can be moved
variantes.contenu_markdown: Geographical mobility is movement from one place to another; occupational mobility is movement from one use or job to another. Land cannot move from place to place, but a plot can be used for farming or for building. Skilled workers often find it hard to change occupation quickly.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When output and the number of workers are given for two periods
variantes.contenu_markdown: Divide output by workers for each period. To compare, subtract the old value from the new one, divide by the old value and multiply by 100.

sections.enonce_markdown:
A bakery in Limbe has six bakers. They bake 1,800 loaves a day. After the owner buys a mixing machine, the same six bakers bake 2,400 loaves a day.
(a) Say which factor of production is the oven, which is the skill and work of the bakers, and which is the owner who decides what to bake and carries the risk of loss.
(b) Calculate the productivity of labour before and after the machine.
(c) Calculate the percentage increase in productivity.
(d) Give one reason for the increase.

etapes.justification: Use the definition of each factor.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The oven is **capital**; the skill and work of the bakers is **labour**; the owner who decides and bears the risk is **enterprise**.

etapes.justification: Divide output by the number of workers.
Same formula with the new output.
Change divided by the old value, times 100.
The number of workers did not change, so something else raised output per worker.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The machine is extra capital, which lets each baker mix more dough in the same time.

sections.conclusion_markdown: (a) Oven: capital; bakers: labour; owner: enterprise. (b) 300 loaves per baker before and 400 after. (c) Productivity rose by 33.3%. (d) The new machine gave each worker more capital to work with.

items.erreur_markdown: "Capital is the money in a person's bank account."
items.pourquoi_faux: In production, capital means the real goods that help to make other goods. Money only buys them.
items.correction_markdown: Capital is the set of man-made goods, such as machines, tools and buildings, used to produce other goods and services.

items.erreur_markdown: "A firm buys labour in the same way as it buys a machine."
items.pourquoi_faux: A worker cannot be separated from his or her labour. The employer cannot own the person.
items.correction_markdown: A firm hires the services of workers for a period and pays wages. Machines can be bought and owned.

items.pourquoi_faux: Land in economics is wider than the soil used for crops.
items.correction_markdown: Land includes all natural resources: soil, forests, rivers, minerals and fishing grounds.

items.erreur_markdown: "The reward for capital is profit, and the reward for enterprise is interest."
items.correction_markdown: Capital earns interest; enterprise earns profit; land earns rent; labour earns wages.

items.erreur_markdown: "Indirect production means producing goods through a middleman."
items.pourquoi_faux: It has nothing to do with middlemen. It describes the order in which things are made.
items.correction_markdown: Indirect production means making capital goods first and using them later to make consumer goods.

items.enonce_markdown: Name the four factors of production and give the reward that each one earns.

A tailoring workshop in Bamenda has 8 workers who sew 960 school uniforms in one month. In the next month 12 workers sew 1,800 uniforms.
(a) Calculate the productivity of labour in each month.
(b) Calculate the percentage change in productivity.
(c) Give two possible causes of the change.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Month 1: $\frac{960}{8} =$ **120 uniforms per worker**. Month 2: $\frac{1\,800}{12} =$ **150 uniforms per worker**.
(b) $\frac{150 - 120}{120} \times 100 =$ **25% increase**.
(c) Training of the workers and better sewing machines, or better organisation of the tasks. Any two reasonable causes earn the marks.

items.enonce_markdown:
A fisherman catches 10 kg of fish a day with a hand line. He decides to stop fishing for 6 days to make a net. With the net he catches 25 kg a day.
(a) Explain how this is an example of indirect production.
(b) Calculate the fish he gives up during the 6 days.
(c) After how many days of fishing with the net does the extra catch make up for what he gave up?
(d) Name the capital good.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) He makes a capital good (the net) first and uses it later to produce fish, a consumer good. He gives up present consumption for greater output in future.
(b) $6 \times 10 =$ **60 kg**.
(c) Extra catch per day $= 25 - 10 = 15$ kg, and $\frac{60}{15} =$ **4 days**.
(d) The **net**.

items_markdown: The four factors are land, labour, capital and enterprise, earning rent, wages, interest and profit.
Land is all natural resources; capital is man-made goods used in production; enterprise organises the other factors and takes risks.
Labour cannot be separated from the worker, so it is hired, not bought and owned like land or capital.
Productivity of labour is output divided by the number of workers; it rises with training, health, tools and motivation.
Indirect production is making capital goods first and using them later to make consumer goods, at the cost of present consumption.
